title: KP14 with a QUADRATIC price of productivity risk: gamma_x x min(1 + 0.25 y^2, 3), y an unpriced stationary state no firm is exposed to
question: Group 2, harmonized with gq25 (GS21): does a price of risk that rises quadratically with the distance of an aggregate state from its mean create room or a gap?
notes: Campaign 2026-10-14. KP14's own states x and z are random walks, so a quadratic in their level is not stationary; the multiplier is a function of the outside state y (kappa 0.35, unit sd), as in kpgam. Form 1 + q s^2 (never below the baseline price) because KP14's growth-option discount turns negative once gamma_x falls below ~0.82 of its value.
